_note: The shipped control library. Each template maps to requirements across every seeded framework; `maps` entries are [framework_key, requirement_key, coverage, rationale]. Coverage: 'full' = this control alone satisfies the requirement; 'partial' = it satisfies part, other controls needed; 'supporting' = it contributes evidence but does not itself satisfy. Honest coverage grading is the point - a library that claims 'full' everywhere produces a green dashboard and a failed audit.

templates.title: Multi-factor authentication on privileged and remote access
templates.objective: All administrative, remote and externally-reachable access requires a second authentication factor.
templates.guidance: Scope must include infrastructure SSH, cloud consoles, VPN, source control and the production database - not only the web application. Break-glass accounts need a documented exception with compensating controls.
maps: Implements the authentication element of logical access security; other controls cover authorisation and boundary protection.
Raises the cost of credential-based attack from outside the system boundary.
Secure authentication is precisely what this control implements.
Governs the handling of authentication information; allocation and lifecycle covered elsewhere.
Constrains how privileged rights may be exercised.
Verifies that the person seeking ePHI access is the one claimed.
A second factor reduces reliance on password strength alone.
Contributes to appropriate technical measures; not sufficient alone.

templates.title: Unique named accounts; no shared or generic credentials
templates.objective: Every actor with system access holds an individually attributable identity.
templates.guidance: Shared accounts break attribution, which silently invalidates audit logging as evidence. Service accounts are permitted but must be owned by a named person.
maps: Identity is the precondition for logical access control.
Registration of users presupposes distinguishable users.
Identity management across the full lifecycle.
Audit controls are unattributable without unique identity.
Contributes to integrity and confidentiality of processing.

templates.title: Role-based access with least privilege and segregation of duties
templates.objective: Access is granted by role, limited to what the role requires, and conflicting duties are separated.
maps: Role-based authorisation, least privilege and segregation of duties are the stated criterion.
Information access restriction per the access control policy.
Covers provisioning and modification; periodic review is a separate control.
Technical access control; authentication and emergency access covered elsewhere.
Supports data minimisation by limiting who may reach personal data.

templates.title: Quarterly access review and recertification
templates.objective: Access rights are reviewed by system owners at least quarterly and revoked where no longer justified.
templates.guidance: The evidence an auditor wants is the completed review with reviewer, date, and the revocations that resulted. A review that never removes anything invites the question of whether it happened.
maps: Credential removal when access is no longer required.
Periodic confirmation that least privilege still holds.
A recurring evaluation of control operation.
Review and modification of access rights.

templates.title: Onboarding and offboarding with same-day access revocation
templates.objective: Access is provisioned on a documented authorisation and fully revoked on the final working day.
maps: Registration and authorisation of new users and removal when no longer required.
Provisioning and removal of access rights.
Return of organisational assets on termination.
Responsibilities that persist after employment ends.
Termination procedures for ending ePHI access.

templates.title: TLS 1.2 or higher on all external interfaces
templates.objective: All data in transit across untrusted networks is encrypted with current protocol versions and valid certificates.
templates.guidance: Continuously monitorable: enumerate public endpoints and assert negotiated version, cipher suite and certificate validity. A redirect to HTTPS is not enforcement if the plaintext port still serves content.
maps: Protects information during transmission and movement.
Applies cryptography in transit; key management and at-rest use covered elsewhere.
Technical measures guarding ePHI transmitted over a network.
Encryption named as an appropriate measure.

templates.title: Encryption at rest for all data stores and backups
templates.objective: Persistent storage holding customer, personal or health data is encrypted, with managed keys.
maps: Protects information assets from security events.
Maintains confidential information in protected form.
Mechanism to encrypt and decrypt ePHI.
Encryption named as an appropriate measure.

templates.title: Centralised, tamper-evident audit logging
templates.objective: Security-relevant events are logged with actor, action, object and time, shipped off-host, and retained per policy.
templates.guidance: Logs that the logged party can edit are not evidence. Ship off the host and restrict deletion.
maps: Supplies the record that anomaly monitoring analyses.
Detective complement to preventive access control.

templates.title: Vulnerability scanning with remediation SLAs
templates.objective: Infrastructure and dependencies are scanned on a schedule; findings are triaged and remediated within severity-based deadlines.
templates.guidance: Reachability matters: an unreachable critical outranks a reachable medium only if you have actually checked reachability. Record the decision either way.
maps: Detection of configuration changes and susceptibility to new vulnerabilities.
Reduces risks to a reasonable and appropriate level.

templates.title: Encrypted backups with periodic restore testing
templates.objective: Backups run on schedule, are encrypted, and are proven recoverable by an actual restore into an isolated environment.
templates.guidance: A backup that has never been restored is an assumption. Assert on restored row counts against the source, not on the exit code of the backup job - a job that silently skipped a database exits zero.

templates.title: Breach assessment and statutory notification procedure
templates.objective: A documented procedure determines notifiability and meets every applicable statutory clock.
templates.guidance: GDPR allows 72 hours to the supervisory authority; HIPAA allows a business associate 60 days to the covered entity. One incident touching both populations runs both clocks, and the plan must be built to the shorter one.

templates.title: Secure development lifecycle with security testing

templates.title: Separated environments; no production data in development or test
templates.objective: Development, test and production are segregated, and production personal data is never copied into lower environments.
templates.guidance: The usual failure is a convenience restore of a production dump into staging. That single act puts real PHI or personal data into an environment with weaker access control.

templates.title: Documented periodic risk assessment and treatment plan
templates.objective: Risks to confidentiality, integrity and availability are identified, scored against defined criteria, assigned owners, and treated under an approved plan.
templates.guidance: For HIPAA this is the control OCR asks about first, and a vulnerability scan does not satisfy it: the assessment must be organisation-wide and reach administrative and physical safeguards too.

templates.title: Named security officer with documented responsibilities

templates.title: Vendor risk assessment with DPA and BAA coverage

templates.guidance: Coverage means the right instrument for the data: a BAA where PHI is involved, a DPA with sub-processor terms where personal data is. A SOC 2 report from the vendor is assurance, not a contract.

templates.title: Data subject request intake and fulfilment within statutory deadlines

templates.guidance: Everything downstream depends on this being complete. An asset absent from the inventory is absent from the risk assessment, the access review and the backup schedule - and nothing will report it missing.

templates.title: Risk-to-control mapping and control design review
templates.objective: Controls are selected and designed against identified risks, the link between each risk and the controls treating it is documented, and the design is reviewed when risks change.
templates.guidance: This is the step between having a risk register and having controls: showing that the control set was chosen to treat the assessed risks rather than copied from a template. ISO calls the output the Statement of Applicability.
